text:
maria: Hey team — Acme (support case T-1234) just reported a big p99 latency spike for the /v1/generate path from US-WEST customers starting ~22:13 PDT. p95 went from ~120ms to ~980ms. I can repro a couple of slow traces. Anyone oncall? :eyes:

kevin: oncall here. pulling graphs now. which subnet/region specifically? customer IPs look like us-west-2.

maria: yes us-west-2. Customer provided curl timings: `time_connect` ~800ms, `time_starttransfer` ~1.1s. They saw multiple TLS handshake slow logs.

ashley: looking at edge metrics — we have a p95 spike on ingress-eu-west -> wait, for us-west we see increased TLS handshake latency on edge-egress-3 between 22:12-22:20. Handshake duration percentiles: p50 60ms, p95 450ms, p99 920ms.

jon: I ran a quick `dig` against our api hostname from an external vantage: `;; Query time: 3 msec` — DNS seems fine. But traceroute from an external probe shows an extra cross-AZ hop:
```
traceroute to api.redwood.example (52.23.45.67), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.3 ms  0.2 ms  0.2 ms
 2  34.120.1.1  2.1 ms  2.0 ms  2.1 ms
 3  * * *
 4  198.51.100.7  180.9 ms  181.0 ms  180.8 ms
 5  52.23.45.67  181.1 ms  180.9 ms  181.0 ms
```
That 180ms hop looks like a hairpin to a different AZ or provider POP.

kevin: hairpin would explain handshake blowup — SYN -> remote -> long RTT -> SYN-ACK -> full handshake elongated. Any recent routing changes?

ops-bot: alert: aws-bgp-flaps detected in us-west-2 between 22:05-22:18, flap_count=7, affected_prefixes=52.23.45.0/24

ashley: correlate that with our internal egress gateways — I see egress-gw-7 switched path at 22:10 and started prefering transit provider B (longer AS path). BGP change + AWS flap could cause suboptimal routing.

jon: grabbed tcpdump on one of the egress gateways: captures show SYN sent, SYN-ACK arrives ~170-190ms later. server completes handshake quickly once packets arrive. So issue is network path, not TLS CPU. snippet:
```
07:22:12.345678 IP client > gateway: SYN seq 0
07:22:12.516890 IP gateway > client: SYN, ACK seq 0 ack 1 (rtt ~171ms)
07:22:12.516912 IP client > gateway: ACK ack 1
```

maria: customer reported intermittent — sometimes fast, sometimes slow. matches flapping.

kevin: immediate mitigation options: 1) failover traffic away from egress-gw-7 (route pin to egress-gw-3/4), 2) temporarily increase DNS weight to prefer another POP, 3) reduce DNS TTL so we can flip quicker. Which is fastest?

jon: fastest is flipping route at our LB layer to prefer healthy egress nodes — we can push a traffic-policy override for us-west within 2-3 minutes. DNS TTL change will take longer and depend on caches.

ashley: I'm OK doing a targeted policy change. risk is minimal — it's per-region, can be rolled back. I'll trigger a config change to pin health-checked egress nodes.

kevin: go for it. also open a ticket with upstream transit provider and with AWS support for the flap.

ashley: rolling the policy now (deploy id `deploy-1975-usw-routing-override`).

ops-bot: deploy-bot: started deploy deploy-1975-usw-routing-override by ashley at 22:28

ashley: done. traffic now pinned away from egress-gw-7 to gw-3/gw-4. monitoring shows p95 dropped from 980ms -> 140ms within 90s. :tada:

edge-monitor-bot: region us-west-2 TLS-handshake p99 back to baseline 210ms at 22:30.

maria: customer confirmed performance improved, thanks. I'll update the ticket and notify them.

kevin: next steps: jon to escalate to transit provider + AWS support (collect BGP dumps), ashley to leave override for 1h then gradually remove, create follow-up postmortem if provider-level root cause. I'll open an internal incident with incident bot.

jon: collecting BGP MRTs and full tcpdumps now, will attach to ticket. noticed `local_pref` change on gw-7 when it switched to transit B; including AS path details.

ashley: config note: we should add an automated fallback that pins to alternate egress on sustained handshake p95 > 300ms for >2min. filing a follow-up task.

kevin: agreed. also add alert for aws-bgp-flap in us-west with lower threshold.

maria: action items assigned: jon -> vendor escalation (aws/transit) [ETA 4h], ashley -> create routing-fallback task + keep override (ETA 1h), kevin -> incident doc and postmortem (ETA 24h), maria -> customer update.

maria: closing loop — customers re-tested, 95th and 99th are back to normal for the time being. will reopen if it recurs. Great triage everyone. :raised_hands:
